I counted the syllables after the obvious elision in "bene esse" (yielding 14 positions total) and assigned quantities by standard rules: long vowels/diphthongs and closed syllables are L, open short vowels are S. The extra short in the third foot reflects the light syllable in "soli" before the following consonant cluster, and the LL in the fourth foot captures the heavy "quom si-". The final SS closes the line without resolution. This produces a regular, performable rhythm consistent with the genre.

which with the normal synaloephe be-ne’ es-se is written as

be ne es = L S S
se so li = L S S
quom si bi = L S S
sit ma le = L S S

the familiar L S S L S S L S S L S S L S S dactylic shape.

position, so – o long, quom – o long/closed, sit – i long by position,
and the synaloephe bene’esse removes the vowel of ne before es. That is
the textbook rendering of the line.
